cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: For Stability’s Sake
cards.instruction: Hide a destabilizing truth because you believe the current balance of power must be protected.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll keep the launch orderly. Leave the director's name on the program; the department heads need someone above them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Her resignation is coming out of the printer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep that copy here. You choose the running order; just leave her at the top. Without her, the heads will each claim the launch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've noticed her empty seat. Now they're asking which of them gives her opening speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll read it on her behalf. Give each head the same length of introduction, in whatever order keeps them content. You set the timings; I'll keep the director's place occupied in the program.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims orderly launch control; A3 yields order and A5 timings/equal introductions while concealing resignation to preserve a director above competing heads.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 resignation causes A3 document containment; B4 observed empty seat and speech bids cause A5 proxy reading and balanced introductions.

relationship.evidence: B2 reports evidence and B4 a real event problem; A incorporates B timing choices to keep the response cooperative.

heightening.evidence: A5 fills the apparent vacancy with representation of the old authority instead of elevating one department head.

specificity.evidence: A1 program, B2 resignation and B4 empty seat establish distinct facts and knowledge.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 program-place phrase is explicit but follows the exact threatened speech role.

coach2.inferred: A believes retaining the director role prevents department heads contesting power.
coach2.missing: No hidden announcement or unseen conversation is required for the heads behavior.
coach2.firstDefect: The third-party knowledge cue is clarified; no mandatory defect identified.

A1-B2.evidence: B2 reveals the destabilizing truth behind A1 retained name.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 contains B2 printout and explains why the balance matters.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 shows the heads responding to observable absence rather than an established resignation disclosure.
